rv.q: There's a lot to like in Mrs. Stern Wanders the Prussian State Library, including literate dialogue and a sharp eye for the methods employed by governments to marginalize and destroy dissent. But it could use a jolt of tension.
In summary, Mrs. Stern Wanders the Prussian State Library is a finely-crafted play that I hope will find a future life.

cn.t: Critics find Bader's play about Hannah Arendt tackles a fascinating historical episode, though execution proves uneven, with one reviewer strongly endorsing the production while another questions whether it fully capitalizes on its compelling subject matter.
